samples.scenario: Spearphishing via Compromised Vendor Email Account to Initiate Fraudulent Payment
samples.technical_data: [Complex structure with keys: email_headers, vendor_domain_dkim_status, smtp_logs, vendor_account_login_history, email_body_content]
indicators: Sudden spike in emails from vendor@examplevendor.com with SPF softfail
Login detected from IP 203.0.113.55 geolocated in Eastern Europe, unusual for vendor
Email contained urgent request to change bank account details for payments
SPF record for vendor domain partially misconfigured, allowing spoofing
Mismatch between sending IP and vendor's known mail servers
Email body requested immediate wire transfer to new foreign bank account
samples.detection_method: Monitor vendor account login patterns and IP geolocations; enforce strict SPF/DKIM/DMARC validation on inbound vendor emails; alert on changes to vendor payment instructions; confirm payment detail changes through established vendor communication channels

samples.scenario: Unauthorized Access to HR Manager's Email Account to Exfiltrate Employee Data via Business Email Compromise
samples.technical_data: [Complex structure with keys: o365_audit_logs, mailbox_access_logs, email_forwarding_rules, email_content_analysis, ip_geolocation_data]
indicators: Unusual mailbox forwarding rule created to external email address
Login from IP 45.77.23.19 located in Southeast Asia not consistent with HR manager travel history
Mass email sent with employee W2 forms attached
Multiple failed login attempts prior to successful access
O365 audit logs show mailbox permission changes
Emails sent contained requests for sensitive personally identifiable information
samples.detection_method: Implement monitoring for mailbox rule changes and external forwarding; alert on logins from new geolocations; conduct regular review of privileged account access; enable anomaly detection on high-volume sensitive data emails; enforce MFA for all accounts with access to PII

samples.scenario: Compromised Executive Assistant Email Used to Send Fraudulent Payment Approval Requests
samples.technical_data: [Complex structure with keys: corporate_email_server_logs, mailflow_headers, login_activity_reports, endpoint_protection_alerts]
indicators: Login to assistant@company.com from IP 192.0.2.123 in South America not matching normal pattern

Email headers show 'Return-Path' mismatch and SPF softfail
Endpoint alert for credential dumping tools detected on assistant's workstation

samples.scenario: Spoofed CEO Email Domain Used to Request Confidential Contracts via Phishing
samples.technical_data: [Complex structure with keys: email_gateway_spf_dkim_reports, dns_records, phishing_email_samples, network_traffic_logs]
indicators: SPF record for ceo@company.com domain returned neutral due to missing include for third-party mail service
DKIM signature missing on spoofed emails
Email sent from IP 198.51.100.150 outside authorized mail server IP range
Email body requested urgent sending of confidential contracts
DNS records showed recently added subdomain mimicking CEO’s address
Network logs showed multiple clicks on embedded phishing links
samples.detection_method: Harden SPF/DKIM/DMARC records and enforce strict fail policies; detect domain shadowing or lookalike subdomains; monitor email gateway for spoofed domain activity; implement user awareness training for executives; verify sensitive document requests through voice confirmation
